title: Old burial jewelry, cemetery fights and the huge second line for Black Benny
summary: Rene recalls people buried with jewelry, fights after funerals between uptown and downtown, and a ten-block-long funeral with second liners dancing on both sides.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: That's right. All that was requested, he wanted to be full dressed. And see, a long time ago when they used to bury people, they used to bury people with all their jewelry. They were watching everything, everything a person desired, they were buried, you see. That's why you take the section, the graveyard section, man, they have so much jewelry, you know. I know a fellow had box of stuff. All kinds of good, nice gold stuff and everything. Another thing too, I'll tell you about the broomsticks, eh? The broomstick section. Well, the fellows used to, you know, they'd meet. If you had a funeral, well most of the funerals in downtown, they would bury them down to go to the Hope's Graveyard, see, or even St. Louis. But a lot of the fights would take place after the funeral, being one of these uptown, you know. Because most of the graveyards would go to downtown, like the Hope's and the St. Louis Cemetery and all that. They used to have a garage cemetery, but very few people was buried there, you know. Very few. Yeah, and like I tell you, the second line, I think the second line was somewhere, he's around 900 or 1,000, behind Black Bennett. They had a funeral about maybe about 10 blocks long, and I think the second line was on both sides of the bank, just like that.
All jammed together, huh? Jammed together.

Jammed together. And still doing the same thing, what you see them doing there. The only thing they used to go to the ground, man, and go around until they fall down, and they'd be on the ground still dancing. Flat on their back, you think. It was a real show, man. It was a real thing. I look at them sometimes. I'd be busy studying, man. Sometimes they'd draw my attention so much I can't help them laughing, you know. The way they do, it's real kicks now, I tell you. Now what else would you like to know if there's something important I know you'd like to know?
